ordering_contract.conclusion: A: strict output order matching accepted input order
ordering_contract.basis: rtl/membrane_quant_stream_top.sv's own header ('---- ordering guarantee ----') states this unconditionally and it is enforced by that file's own live `ifndef SYNTHESIS assertions, and by every existing differential testbench's own single-FIFO-order inflight-deque check. Confirmed from source, not assumed. See results/b2-stall-root-cause.md section 0.

scheduler_architecture.mechanism: global monotonic issue-sequence-number tag (SEQ_WIDTH=8 bits) assigned to every transaction at issue; a transaction may write to the shared output FIFO only when its own seq equals a free-running next_retire_seq counter
scheduler_architecture.q8_encode: single-in-flight (unchanged discipline), one hold register for its own completed-but-not-yet-its-turn result
scheduler_architecture.q4_encode: single-in-flight (unchanged discipline), one hold register, now issued independently of Q8_0 encode (no longer mutually exclusive with it, unlike Phase B1)
scheduler_architecture.tag_pipe_q8dec_q4dec: unchanged fixed-latency shared shift register (L_MAX=7), NEVER stalled/frozen (stalling it would lose in-flight q8_dequantize/q4_unpack results with no ready/valid backpressure of their own -- see phase-b2.md); a shared SHADOW_DEPTH-entry (1 or 2) hold queue catches the bounded number of tag_pipe entries admitted while an older Q8_0/Q4_0 encode transaction is still outstanding
scheduler_architecture.reorder_buffer: none built -- explicitly smaller than every configuration EXP-FPGA-DIV-001 Phase B3 already evaluated and rejected

correctness_full_run.scope_note: correctness scope includes deliberately adversarial stress stages (long Q8_0-encode bursts, Q8_0-encode-then-long-Q4_0-decode-burst, three alternating patterns, dense random-mode heavy-backpressure, queue-full boundary, reset in every externally-observable scheduler state) -- its own aggregate cycles/transaction number is NOT the basis for the item-8 collateral-slowdown/improvement thresholds, which use the performance-matrix profiles instead (results/b2-performance.csv) since those isolate specific, controlled traffic shapes

ordering_and_drop_checks.note: internal assertion firings checked by grepping all four run logs for this module's own $error message prefix -- none found, across all four (baseline has no such assertions to fire; B1's and B2's own live `ifndef SYNTHESIS assertions, compiled in via Verilator --assert, never fired)

sequence_tag_wraparound.note: real wraparound coverage from scale alone, not a special-cased scenario -- the live_seq_count assertion (module-internal, checks issue_seq_ctr - next_retire_seq computed at the SAME 8-bit modular width, not width-promoted) never fired across any of the four full runs
